steps.content:
It is the Rust, and it is a dump.
Filthy water flows openly, and awful smells fill your nose.
There are always pairs of eyes peering out from the dark places. With ill-intent, they track every stranger who sets foot in this region.
In order to investigate Hank's cause of death, you and Wolverine have come to his home, hoping that you will be able to find some clue among his belongings.

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: We're here, it's that tent up ahead.
He calls it a tent, but it's more like a bunch of rags supported on some wooden sticks, shaking perilously in the rotten wind.

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: Only the two of us? Aren't they coming along?
Wolverine glances at the guards stationed not far off.

options: Right, the two of us are enough.
They have other things to do.

choices.text: Right, the two of us are enough.
They have other things to do.

steps.content: It doesn't look that dangerous here. We don't need to call in the cavalry.
And it's not like you enjoy dealing with them anyway.
And right, don't forget you've promised...

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: I know, not to hurt anyone... so annoying.

As you step deeper, you feel the smell is enough to make your hair stand on end. There's rotten and stinky food, the ground is covered with filthy blackened clumps, and everyday items are piled in a corner. It's like a miniature dump.

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: These are the old bastard's clothes. Sometimes he would hide little things in his waistband.
Wolverine kicks some nearby rags, and Pippy raises his head to sniff them. He freezes, lets out a clear "O!" and hurries back to hide behind Wolverine.

Wolverine doesn't seem bothered. He searches through the trash intently. You see something bright flash out of the corner of your eye, and you follow the light to its source. It is a distorted steel basin.
It looks like a steel basin...

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: The old man washed food and bathed in it.
All in the same basin?

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: Of course. When he found me at the Rust, he used it to...

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: Well, forget it... It's not important...

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: Enough talk. Don't you have your work to do?
Wolverine turns his head away, avoiding your searching gaze. He continues digging through the trash.

options: Is there something you're looking for?

choices.text: Is there something you're looking for?

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: I... I just hate that you're going so slow!
Really?

Hank's belongings are messy and scattered. After a long time of searching, you haven't found anything. Just when you're ready to leave this reeking place to get some fresh air, a shadow appears in front of you.
Yo yo yo, isn't it that Wolverine who got sold to the gang? It's me! Don't you remember me? I'm Labiche! I used to live nearby!
When he hears the voice, Wolverine's steps slow down. He glares at him and walks right up.

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: Get out of here, I don't know you.

steps.speaker: Labiche
steps.content:
Don't be like that! I held you when you were found.
Oh, we have an honored guest here. Friend, may I know...
Labiche turns his flattering gaze toward you. You know how sensitive the MBCC is, so you vaguely tell him that—

steps.speaker: Labiche
steps.content: Ho ho, the cub has really latched onto a big shot, huh?

steps.speaker: Labiche
steps.content: Ho ho, how could we have someone as fancy as you passing by here? You must be some big shot the cub has latched onto.

steps.speaker: Labiche
steps.content: Look at that weapon, those clothes, and that fat, white little pet... Tsk tsk, you've been living the good life! No wonder you never came back to see us.

steps.speaker: Labiche
steps.content: Friend, let me tell you. Forget how clean he is now—when he was little, he was a little animal scrambling through the Rust basin. Naked, consorting every day with Corruptor monsters—he couldn't even speak!

steps.speaker: Labiche
steps.content: All he could say was ook ook, aa aa aha ha ha ha—

steps.speaker: Pippy
steps.content: Hiss!
None of what Labiche is saying is particularly kind. Even Pippy feels uncomfortable, baring his teeth at him.

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: Stop jabbering and stay out of our way!

steps.speaker: Labiche
steps.content: Out of your way? Maybe I could be your help! Friend, you came here for Hank, right?
On hearing Hank's name, Wolverine raises his question eagerly.

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: You know where Hank is? He's still alive, isn't he!

steps.speaker: Labiche
steps.content: Alive? He's been dead a while. I was there when he was found. He was stone cold, that man, buried in a hurry by two security officers.
You have confirmed multiple times that Hank is actually dead, but still do not know the reason.

steps.speaker: Labiche
steps.content: You want to know how old Hank died? You've come to the right person, friend!
You have confirmed multiple times that Hank is actually dead, but still do not know the reason. Perhaps there is a clue in what Labiche saw...

steps.speaker: Labiche
steps.content: You've come to the right person, friend! I got a good look at every wound on Hank's body.
Seemingly disinterested, Wolverine pricks up his ears to listen closely to Labiche.

steps.speaker: Labiche
steps.content: I've been a scavenger along the Rust for years. I've seen it a million times before. I'm sure he was killed by Corruptors.
Corruptors?

steps.speaker: Labiche
steps.content: Right! The weird thing is he had a ton of injuries. There were flesh and guts everywhere...

steps.speaker: Labiche
steps.content: Living in the Rust basin for that long, the old guy had to have a lot of skill, so there must have been a crazy number of Corruptors to rip him up like that!

steps.speaker: Labiche
steps.content: Back then when he sold this little animal, he didn't share a coin of what he earned with us. Ha, guess he deserves it!
Was there anything suspicious about his death?

steps.speaker: Labiche
steps.content: Isn't that many Corruptors killing one old guy suspicious enough? I didn't see one piece of skin left whole on Old Hank, it's like they're revenging or something! I'd say he was punished for what he had done before!
While you're still thinking through this, Wolverine's veins have begun to bulge.
Pippy also seems to feel his master's anger and looks worriedly at Wolverine. Only Labiche continues his monologue as if he hasn't noticed anything.

steps.speaker: Labiche
steps.content:
Finding this little beast made him so proud, he taught him how to speak and the so-called meaning of life.
That **** was always talking about "the Meaning of Life," but he was trampled by Corruptors in the end, he deserves it, hahaha...

steps.speaker: Labiche
steps.content: Ah—!
Before you can react, Wolverine has already punched the scavenger's face.

steps.speaker: Labiche
steps.content: What's wrong with you, you little beast!
Wolverine is shaking with rage.

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: Stop laughing! Is this funny to you?

steps.speaker: Labiche
steps.content: When was I laughing at you? Oh... you still don't like being called a little beast.

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: Hank is dead! Do you think this is funny?!

steps.speaker: Labiche
steps.content: Huh? Of course it's...

steps.speaker: Labiche
steps.content: Aah!
Wolverine hits Labiche again, and throws him to the ground.
Stop! Before we left, you promised me you wouldn't hurt anyone!
Wolverine is too furious to listen to you. He chokes Labiche and slams his head against the ground, then punches him again.

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: I'll show you funny!
Another punch, and you hear a sharp cracking sound from Labiche's nose.

steps.speaker: Labiche
steps.content: Help... Friend... help...

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: Show you funny!
Labiche's front teeth have been knocked out, and he's out of breath to call for help. The thick smell of blood mixes with the rotten stench of the dump.
Wolverine, stop! You'll kill him!

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: I want to kill him!
Wolverine has no intention of staying his hand, cruelly raining down blow after blow on Labiche's head and body. Labiche's bones make a series of cracking noises and sag deeply.
Wolverine, stop!
Deep red shackles cover Wolverine and bind him, devouring the scarlet in his eyes.
The shackles force him to stop punching, but he still struggles against them.

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: Let me go! I want to kill him!
He lets out angry growls and tries to break free from the shackles. All he is thinking of is pouncing again on the already-dying Labiche.

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: Get out of here! This has nothing to do with you!
Wolverine pushes away from you and continues to torment the dying scavenger.
By the time Hecate sees the red light of the shackles and brings guards, Labiche is practically a corpse.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Sinner S-076 attempted to kill a civilian in the Rust—vile behavior. Chief, according to the rules, he needs to be locked up...

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: So do it. Wouldn't that be just right?
He has no intention of defending himself and is not giving you a chance to explain things to him.

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content:
I see it now, you aren't any different from those gang bastards.
You just want a dog on a leash who won't bite. You're just using me!

options: Why did you want to kill him?

choices.text: Why did you want to kill him?

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: How could I!

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: Hank fed me, clothed me, taught me to speak! He was the first person to treat me like a human being!

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: Even when he was starving, he would put aside a mouthful of soup for me!

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: Hank is different from this bastard, the gang dog trainers, and the people in the Bureau!

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: And he would never put me in such shackles!

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: I won't let anyone laugh at him or insult him!

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: Because he deserved it! I won't allow trash like that to insult Hank!
Isn't Hank your enemy, who sold you to the gang?

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: But he was also the only one who ever treated me like a human being!

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: Hank fed me, clothed me, and taught me how to speak! Even when he was starving himself, he'd set aside a mouthful of soup for me!

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: Hank is different from this bastard, the gang dog trainers, and the people in the Bureau!

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: And he would never put me in such shackles!

This is the first time you've heard Wolverine speak so much at once.
Now you not only know Hank's significance to him but also realize his complaints about you.
I never intend to control you. I was trying to stop you from making another wrong choice.

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: I wasn't wrong!
Murder is wrong!

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: He deserved to die!
He was extremely rude, but you can't let yourself be controlled by your emotions. You have to respect ethics and the law!

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: What do ethics and the law have to do with me!
Of course they have to do with you. You said you don't like being called a dog or a monster, right?
I believe that hunting Corruptors was a matter of survival for you, but if I had just let you kill him today, you'll be considered all the more as just a mad dog who bites anyone you see.
If you can't control your own emotions, body, and killing instinct, then you will only ever be a wild beast, and will never be considered a human being.
Wolverine stares at the floor and clenches his fist angrily, but stops struggling. His fingernails are digging into his palms.
Now, calm down. Violence doesn't solve anything.

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: It's none of your damn business! Let me go!
Okay, I can release the shackles. But you know, if you had really killed that scavenger today, you would be considered a wild beast.

steps.speaker: Wolverine
steps.content: I don't want to listen to your crap...
The difference between a human being and a monster is that humans are limited by the law and ethics.
Don't you want people to stop calling you beast and treating you like a dog?
But if you can't control your own emotions, body, and killing instinct, then you will only ever be a wild beast, and will never be considered a human being.

Wolverine opens his mouth a few times, but ends up saying nothing. Lowering his head, he stares at the ground and angrily clenches his fists, but stops struggling at last. His fingernails are digging into his palms.
You hear a voice from far away, as Hecate calls the guards here.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Chief, there was a red flash just now. You were using your ability...
Hecate stops her words. The blood all over the ground, the comatose Labiche and the Wolverine restrained by the shackles... The situation is obvious.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Sinner S-076 has hurt a civilian and must be dealt with severely.
Wolverine is still staring stunned at the ground, processing what you just said.
I will teach and discipline Wolverine personally. Nothing to worry about.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Understood... Any progress in the investigation of the Corruptor trade?
Hm... Have you ever heard of a whole lot of Corruptors in the Rust banding together to attack one person?

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Corruptor attacks don't follow any pattern. They normally just happen.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: A few Corruptors attacking are enough to kill an ordinary person with no special ability.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: A whole lot of Corruptors attacking the same target... You think someone was controlling them?
The scavenger is about to be in serious trouble. We should get him to medical treatment first.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: OK. And S-076...
I will teach and discipline Wolverine personally. Now I have something more important for you.
Going by that scavenger's story, Hank's death was strange indeed.
If Hank was an old man with no special ability, a few Corruptors would have been enough to kill him. Why did so many attack him?

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: You suspect someone is controlling Corruptors?
I'm not sure yet. We do need to look into everything in this place carefully again.
Hecate immediately takes the staff to clean up the scene.
Without saying a word, Wolverine watches them carry Labiche away and pack up Hank's belongings. He looks a bit nostalgic.

After all, this was where he had lived.
His first "home."
